topStories.headline: Two Men Killed in Bayview Within Days of Each Other; Victims Identified
topStories.dek: The San Francisco Medical Examiner has named the two men fatally shot in separate Bayview-Hunters Point incidents on October 1 and October 4, rattling a neighborhood that had seen gun violence drop to historic lows.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Medical Examiner's office has identified the two men killed in back-to-back shootings in Bayview-Hunters Point at the start of October. The victims are 44-year-old Jose Juan Ramirez-Sanchez, who was shot and killed on October 1 near the Yosemite Slough waterfront on Thomas Avenue, and 20-year-old Phillip Leo Jones IV, who was shot and killed on October 4 at Reuel Court in the Ridgeview Terrace housing complex. No arrests have been made in either case.

At the Bayview Station's monthly community meeting on Tuesday, October 7, station captain Bernadette Robinson told attendees that the two shootings are being treated as isolated and independent crimes, and that each likely resulted from a fight that turned violent. Robinson added that outside of the recent incidents, crime in the district remains at a historic low.

The double homicide has nonetheless shocked the neighborhood. In the past two years, gun violence in Bayview-Hunters Point had dropped to an all-time low after decades in which it held some of the highest homicide rates in San Francisco. The October 4 shooting at Ridgeview Terrace is the city's 21st homicide of the year to date, and the sixth in the Bayview neighborhood in 2026.

Anyone with information on either case is asked to contact the SFPD Homicide Detail. Tips can be submitted anonymously through the SFPD tip line at 415-575-4444 or by texting TIP411.

topStories.headline: PG&E Outage Knocks Out Power to Nearly 2,700 Customers in Bayview and Visitacion Valley
topStories.dek: An unplanned blackout struck Bayview and Visitacion Valley on October 6, the latest in a year of recurring outages testing southeastern San Francisco's aging electrical grid.
topStories.body:
A large, unplanned PG&E power outage hit Bayview and Visitacion Valley on Tuesday morning, October 6, leaving roughly 2,694 customers in the dark across San Francisco's southeastern neighborhoods. The disruption was first flagged in an alert from the San Francisco Department of Emergency Management, which was reposted by SFMTA.

The October 6 outage is the latest in what residents and officials have described as a persistent pattern of blackouts in 2026. Just days earlier, on October 1, a separate unplanned PG&E outage cut power to more than 3,000 customers in the Tenderloin and Western Addition. Residents affected by outages can monitor restoration status and sign up for alerts through PG&E's outage center, and can call 1-800-743-5002 for current outage details. PG&E outage information is available in English, Spanish, Chinese, and Tagalog.

topStories.headline: Excelsior Gears Up for Its Biggest Weekend of the Year: Block Party, Lucha Libre, and Salvadoran Heritage Week
topStories.dek: Sunday Streets returns to the Excelsior on October 18 with a car-free block party packed with cultural events, while a week of Salvadoran heritage programming on Mission Street begins October 14.
topStories.body:
The Excelsior's most festive stretch of the year is underway. The Excelsior Community Block Party — the final Sunday Streets event of the 2026 season — takes place Sunday, October 18, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Mission Street between Geneva Avenue and Theresa Street. The free, all-ages event features a Lucha Libre showcase and Salvi Soul Sunday, a celebration of music, dancing, and art hosted by Salvadoran Soul Encuentro, along with the full Sunday Streets lineup of active-play games, health resources, and live music.

For those who want to start the day on foot, SF Crosstown Trails and Livable City are co-hosting a guided three-mile neighborhood walk beginning at 9:30 a.m. at Cayuga Playground Park on Alemany Boulevard near Naglee Avenue, winding through historic spots before ending at the block party. The Excelsior Branch Library, at 4400 Mission St., is also joining in with an open house that day featuring live musical performances, a chess tournament, and sidewalk chalk drawing.

In the days leading up to Sunday Streets, Salvadoran Soul Encuentro is presenting a series of events along the Mission Street corridor celebrating Salvadoran heritage. The schedule includes a night of Salvadoran storytelling on Wednesday, October 14, and a poetry and vinyl record showcase on Friday, October 16, both at Casa De Apoyo, 4834 Mission St., beginning at 6 p.m.

moreNews.headline: SF Agency Picks Oakdale Avenue for Long-Awaited Bayview Caltrain Station
moreNews.body: After nearly four decades of planning, the San Francisco County Transportation Authority has settled on Oakdale Avenue and Third Street as the preferred location for a new Caltrain station in Bayview. The recommendation, finalized this summer following a 2026 study, found that the Oakdale site consistently outscored an alternative on Evans Avenue in projected ridership, climate resilience, accessibility, and cost — an Evans location would have cost an estimated $120 million more to build. The Paul Avenue Caltrain station, the neighborhood's last stop, closed in 2005. A final report is expected in fall 2026; planners caution it may be a decade before construction begins, though roughly $27 million from the 2022 Proposition L sales tax is already set aside for design and planning.

moreNews.headline: Small Change Arcade Set to Open on Mission Street
moreNews.body: Small Change Arcade, a nonprofit community arcade at 4740 Mission Street in the Excelsior, is set to open this month. Owner Matthew Sengbusch, who builds custom miniature arcade cabinets from vintage original hardware, announced a grand opening on October 16. The arcade is one of three 2026 Storefront Opportunity Grant recipients in the Excelsior and will feature 15 pinball machines and classic arcade games, along with programming including tournaments and youth activities.

moreNews.headline: Green Space Coming to Vacant Third Street Lot in Bayview
moreNews.body: A temporary green space is coming to the vacant corner lot at Jerrold Avenue and Third Street in Bayview-Hunters Point. Economic Development on Third Street (EDOT) is partnering with Climate Action Now! to bring free pavement removal and garden support to the site, according to Mission Local's October 7 Bayview Buzz column. The project is part of ongoing efforts to activate underused parcels along the Third Street corridor.

restaurants.name: Old Skool Cafe
restaurants.description: A 1920s jazz-themed supper club and violence-prevention nonprofit employing at-risk youth ages 16–22, serving Southern soul food with live jazz Wed–Sat evenings.

restaurants.name: Gumbo Social
restaurants.description: Build-your-own gumbo, po'boys, and Cajun-Creole small plates from chef-owner Dontaye Ball, one of Bayview's Third Street anchors; reopened August 17 after a planned summer refresh.

restaurants.name: Smoke Soul Kitchen
restaurants.description: Black- and woman-owned brunch counter in the former Auntie April's space serving fried chicken, waffles, shrimp and grits, and house-made biscuits Wed–Sun.

restaurants.name: Frank Grizzly's
restaurants.description: Family-owned taqueria celebrated for birria tacos, duck tacos, and quesabirria, now settled into its own Bayview brick-and-mortar after launching at Anchor Brewing.

restaurants.name: The Old Clam House
restaurants.description: San Francisco's oldest restaurant in its original location (est. 1861), serving steamed clams, cioppino, Dungeness crab, and house-made pastas under the Florese family since 2022.

restaurants.name: All Good Pizza
restaurants.description: Brick-oven Neapolitan pizzas, organic salads, and paninis served in a 7,000-sq-ft Bayview beer garden using locally sourced, seasonal ingredients.

restaurants.name: Cafe Alma
restaurants.description: Waterfront café in a 5,000-sq-ft India Basin warehouse serving locally sourced breakfast and lunch Tue–Sat, doubling as a community event, workshop, and live-music venue.

restaurants.name: Gratta Wines
restaurants.description: Bayview's own garage winery producing hand-crafted Dry Creek wines since 2006, with a tasting room, wine bar, and Italian specialty market on Third Street.

restaurants.name: Yvonne's Southern Sweets
restaurants.description: Beloved Bayview institution (est. 2002) selling small-batch pecan pralines, red velvet cupcakes, lemon meringue pies, and butter pecan cookies; reopened this fall and celebrates 20 years on Oct. 4.

restaurants.name: Drew's Barbecue
restaurants.description: Tucked-away Visitacion Valley destination widely praised as the best BBQ in San Francisco, serving ribs, chicken, hot links, and sides Thu–Sat.

restaurants.name: La Joya Café
restaurants.description: Visitacion Valley neighborhood staple on Leland Avenue serving fresh chilaquiles, breakfast burritos, handmade tacos, and espresso drinks made to order daily.

restaurants.name: Pho Luen Fat
restaurants.description: Long-running Leland Avenue standby serving Vietnamese pho, ho fun, Chinese BBQ plates, and Cantonese noodles at affordable neighborhood prices.

restaurants.name: Calabria Brothers
restaurants.description: Excelsior Italian deli beloved for enormous, generously stuffed sandwiches and charcuterie at lunch-counter prices.

restaurants.name: Ty Sandwich
restaurants.description: Excelsior go-to for fresh bánh mì packed with quality ingredients and fast, friendly service at very affordable prices.

restaurants.name: Don Chuy's Mexi-Mercado
restaurants.description: Excelsior corner market with a small kitchen turning out carnitas burritos, quesadillas, and enchiladas that regulars rank among the neighborhood's best.

restaurants.name: Pho Golden
restaurants.description: Highly rated Excelsior restaurant for fragrant pho, noodle soups, and Vietnamese comfort dishes at everyday prices.

restaurants.name: Tala Wine
restaurants.description: Boutique Excelsior wine bar founded by Tala Drzewiecki, curating low-intervention natural wines from small French, Spanish, and Italian producers, with snack plates and tea service.

restaurants.name: The Halfway Club
restaurants.description: Midwestern-inspired Crocker-Amazon bar and restaurant with cult-status chili cheese fries, stiff cocktails, and movie nights — a James Beard Best New Bar semifinalist.

restaurants.name: Restaurante Familiar
restaurants.description: Casual Excelsior sit-down restaurant specializing in pupusas, Salvadoran entrées, and Mexican plates in a family-friendly setting.

restaurants.name: Hawaiian Drive Inn
restaurants.description: Fast, affordable Hawaiian plate lunch spot on Mission Street serving kalua pork, teriyaki chicken, and loco moco to Excelsior regulars.

restaurants.name: Super Star Restaurant
restaurants.description: Long-established Excelsior takeout staple serving Filipino and Chinese home-cooked lunch plates at some of the lowest prices on Mission Street.

shops.name: Gratta Wines Italian Market

shops.name: Oxbridge Market

artEntertainment.name: The Midway
artEntertainment.description: Sprawling 40,000-sq-ft Bayview venue hosting EDM concerts, queer parties, and live events, with upcoming shows including Chief Keef (Oct. 23) and Valentino Khan (Nov. 13).

artEntertainment.name: JOY Gallery
